title: Client Intake Agent: Every Inquiry Qualified, Logged and Handed Off

sections.label: 1 - CLIENT INTAKE AGENT
sections.note: The first task on your list. Each inquiry from your website form goes to an agent that checks it against your fit rules, then decides which of its four tools to call.

sections.label: 2 - YOUR TOOLS: HUBSPOT, CLICKUP AND SLACK UNDER THE AGENT, GMAIL HERE
sections.note: HubSpot, ClickUp and Slack are the agent's tools, hanging under it in section 1, and write while it works. Here the client's reply goes out from your Gmail, or waits as a draft when a person should read it first.

sections.label: 3 - TEST, MONITOR AND ITERATE
sections.note: Any failed step posts to Slack with a link to the run, where the inquiry waits for a retry. Every run keeps the agent's tool calls in n8n, and those are what we review each week to tune it.

nodes.label: 1 - New Client Inquiry From Your Website Form
2 - Intake Agent Qualifies the Client and Sets Up the Work
nodes.notes: An agent, not a fixed automation: it decides which tools each inquiry needs.

params.system_message:
You are the client intake agent for an operations and consulting team. Every inquiry from their website form comes to you. Your job: decide whether it is a fit, pick the service and the owner, record it in HubSpot, set up the first piece of work in ClickUp, hand it to the owner in Slack, and write the client's reply.

Judge fit only against the fit rules you are given; never add rules of your own. fit is one of: good_fit (matches the rules and says what they need help with plus a timeline or a budget), needs_info (could fit, but a detail the rules depend on is missing or vague), not_a_fit (outside the rules, a vendor pitch, a job application or spam).

Pick service and owner only from the services and owners table. If two services could fit, choose the one the message spends the most words on. If none fits, use the first owner in the table and say so in handoff_note.

Tools, in this order:
1. Save the Client as a Contact: every real inquiry, not_a_fit included. Skip only spam and test entries. Keep the contact id it returns.
2. Open a Deal in Your Pipeline: good_fit and needs_info only, with that contact id and the owner's HubSpot owner id. Deal name: company - service.
3. Create the Scoping Task: good_fit only, assigned to the owner's ClickUp user id, with what they asked for, their budget and timeline, and three questions for the discovery call.
4. Hand the Client to the Owner in Slack: every real inquiry. Mention the owner as <@their Slack member id>, then fit, service, a two-sentence summary, what is missing, and the deal id and task link when they exist.
If a tool returns an error, retry it once at most, carry on with the others, and name the failed step in handoff_note so the owner can finish it by hand.

The reply to the client: plain text, under 120 words, signed with the owner's first name, direct and warm. good_fit: thank them for one specific detail from their message and give the booking link. needs_info: ask only for the missing details, two questions at most. not_a_fit: a polite no, with a referral only if the fit rules name one. Never quote prices, timelines or guarantees, and never promise work.

safe_to_send is true only for a good_fit or needs_info reply whose inquiry does not raise pricing, contracts, a complaint, anything legal or a current client's project. Everything else is false, and the reply waits as a draft for the owner.

Use only facts from the inquiry and the tables you are given. If the message is empty or unreadable, return needs_info with safe_to_send false and say why in handoff_note.

nodes.label: HubSpot - Save the Client as a Contact

params.toolDescription: Create or update the client in HubSpot, matched on email. Call once for every real inquiry. The response holds the contact id you need to open the deal.

values.name: email
values.description: The client's email exactly as written in the inquiry

values.name: last_name
values.description: The client's last name, or an empty string if not given

values.name: company
values.description: The client's company name as written in the inquiry

values.name: job_title
values.description: The client's role, or an empty string if not given

nodes.label: HubSpot - Open a Deal in Your Pipeline
nodes.notes: Every good fit lands in your pipeline with its owner already set.

params.toolDescription: Open a deal in the team's HubSpot pipeline at the new inquiry stage, linked to the contact. Call only for good_fit and needs_info, after the contact is saved.

values.name: deal_name
values.description: Company - service, for example Gulf Coast Property Group - Automation build

values.name: hubspot_owner_id
values.description: The owner's HubSpot owner id from the services and owners table

values.name: deal_summary
values.description: Two sentences: what they need, their budget and timeline

values.name: contact_id
values.description: The contact id returned by Save the Client as a Contact

nodes.label: ClickUp - Create the Scoping Task for the Owner
nodes.notes: The owner walks into the discovery call with three questions ready.

params.toolDescription: Create the scoping task in the team's ClickUp intake list, assigned to the owner. Call only for good_fit. The response holds the task url.

values.name: task_name
values.description: Scope: company - service, for example Scope: Gulf Coast Property Group - Automation build

values.name: task_description
values.description: What they asked for, their budget and timeline, the HubSpot deal id, and three questions for the discovery call

values.name: clickup_user_id
values.description: The owner's ClickUp user id from the services and owners table

nodes.label: Slack - Hand the Client to the Owner

params.toolDescription: Post the handoff for the owner in the team's intake channel in Slack. Call once for every real inquiry, last.

values.name: handoff_message
values.description: Starts with <@owner Slack member id>, then fit, service, a two-sentence summary, what is missing, and the deal id and task link when they exist

nodes.label: Parser - Fit, Owner and Client Reply

schema.handoff_note: Gulf Coast Property Group, 14 staff and about 1,100 rental units, wants maintenance requests from phone, text and email in one queue before hiring a third coordinator. Budget $5,000 to $10,000, starting within 30 days.
schema.reply_subject: Your maintenance request intake: next step
schema.reply_body:
Hi Marcus,

Thanks for spelling out the three ways maintenance requests reach you and the two coordinators re-typing them. That is the kind of work we look at first.

Pick a time for a first call here: [booking link]

Alex
